issues.summary: Tenderly simulation calls getReadOnlyCurrentGnosisSafeContract without scope, which now throws under a mounted SafeScopeProvider
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: safeContracts.ts:41-45 now calls getAndValidateSafeSDK(scope), which throws when hasActiveScope() (sdk.ts:44-49). tenderly/utils.ts:41 still passes only params.safe, so simulation in a scoped flow (for example ConfirmProposedTx under a scope, which the PR says is supported) will throw.

issues.summary: The scope object gets a new identity on every poll because isFetching is a memo dependency, so scope-dependent effects re-run
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: SafeScopeProvider.tsx:139 includes isFetching in the deps. It toggles on each 15s poll, so the memo returns a new scope twice per poll. ConfirmProposedTx.tsx:29, SafeTxProvider and useTxActions depend on `scope`, so createExistingTx refetches and replaces safeTx during review. The poll test checks only values, never identity, so it cannot catch this.

issues.summary: ConfirmProposedTx under a scope stores an error before the SDK resolves, and nothing clears it afterwards
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: With `initial`, the scope exists but scope.sdk is undefined at first, so createTx→getAndValidateSafeSDK(scope) throws and setSafeTxError is called (ConfirmProposedTx.tsx:29). The only place that clears the error is SafeTxProvider.tsx:112, and it returns early when !canEdit or the nonce and gas match, so the stale TxCheckError banner and the _103 log remain. No test covers this.

issues.summary: dispatchTxExecution gets signerNonce from the URL-chain provider even in a scoped flow
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: dispatch.ts:307 calls getUserNonce, which reads getWeb3ReadOnly(), the URL chain (web3.ts:58-60), even when scope is on another chain. The value is sent in the PROCESSING event and reused by SpeedUpModal:83 as txOptions.nonce. Some claimed details are wrong: txOptions.nonce is not set from it here, and SimpleTxWatcher does not compare nonces.

issues.summary: A provider that is mounted but has no Safe selected yet exposes scope undefined, the same as having no provider, so hooks fall back to the URL/Redux Safe
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: SafeScopeProvider.tsx:123 returns undefined when there is no target, and context.ts:10 cannot tell this apart from no provider. So useSafeInfo and the other hooks use their Safe-level branch until a Safe is selected. Signing is still blocked by the hasActiveScope throw, which limits the impact to displayed data.

issues.summary: The bare catch in runExecutionPreChecks swallows the missing-scope guard throw and silently skips BAD_SIGNATURE
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: executionPreChecks.ts:136-141 catches every error from getAndValidateSafeSDK, including the _822 throw. It is still logged but the check is skipped. The only caller, useTxActions, passes scope, and on-chain execution would still revert with GS026, so the impact is small.

issues.summary: The new scope branch and try/catch in executionPreChecks have no tests
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: executionPreChecks.test.ts is unchanged and mocks only getSafeSDK. useTxActions.scope.test.tsx:27-28 mocks runExecutionPreChecks away completely, so nothing tests whether scope.sdk is used or whether the guard error is swallowed.

issues.summary: Unscoped provider paths (getSafeProvider() and the other read-only contract getters) have no scope parameter or active-scope guard
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: sdk.ts:69-80: getSafeProvider() without scope silently returns the URL-chain provider, with no hasActiveScope check. The multisend, signMessageLib and other getters in safeContracts.ts use it. These are Safe-level paths today, and multisend is planned for WA-3152.

issues.summary: getGnosisSafeContract falls back to the URL-Safe SDK for the version when safe.version is null
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safeContracts.ts:28-31 calls getSafeSDK() without the guard, and the scoped dispatchTxRelay can reach it. The PR's Risks section documents this, and it only affects unsupported mastercopies.

issues.summary: The active-scope guard is a process-wide counter, not tied to the React tree
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: activeScope.ts:8 is a module-global count, so any unscoped getAndValidateSafeSDK anywhere throws while a provider is mounted. The PR describes this as intended, but it would break Safe-level UI that shares the page with a Space flow.

issues.summary: The dynamic import of web3 has no .catch, the same gap as the existing useInitWeb3
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: SafeScopeProvider.tsx:65-68 has no rejection handler, so a failed chunk load leaves web3ReadOnly undefined and no error is reported. useInitWeb3.ts:34 has the same pattern and predates the PR.

issues.summary: The safe-scope barrel has no importers, and it re-exports the heavy provider
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: grep finds no imports of '@/components/tx-flow/safe-scope'. Every consumer deep-imports /context or /types, and comments say this is deliberate for bundle size, so the barrel is dead code and could draw heavy deps into any future importer.

issues.summary: The global bundle grew by 1.24 KB

issues.evidence: Bundle-analyzer output is not available locally. The hooks now import context.ts, which is lightweight, and that likely accounts for the small growth.
